clusters.name: Jonah's move to the conservatory, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: In September 1991 you left home for the conservatory and leaned hard on your closest friend Rafe, but within weeks a wrist injury stopped your playing. By November you had a blow-up with Rafe and he moved out; you were then on your own, getting high, absorbed in fixing radios. By early 1992 you were lost and low, unable to get going, with your grandfather's death in June and your mother's remarriage in the autumn narrowing your footing further. The shifts pile up around your first term away and the injury that ended your music, and the period settles as you earned money fixing radios in the spring.

clusters.name: Jonah's burnout in performance and move from Thornbury, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around September 2001 you began running out of steam for performing and found yourself less content by the month; within a year came a disastrous audition and you were done with the stage, casting about for what came next. In the same months your grandmother was found to have bowel cancer. By late 2002 you were on poor terms with family and friends, left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, met Marisol at a winter party, moved to Fenwick to live with her, then split within the year. Once back in Thornbury that winter you sank into a deep depression and could not face your family; your anxiety rose and you relied, gingerly, on friends. The shifts pile up around your burnout, the failed audition, your grandmother's illness, and the failed relationship, settling gradually as you began to seek help from your parents and returned to your therapist.

clusters.name: Jonah's cutoff from his mother and move to nursing school, 2008–2009
clusters.reason: In January 2008 your grandmother Lorna died; within months you began entry courses at the community college. That July you took four weeks building with Silas at Alder Creek and found yourself too drained for conversation with your mother; she pushed to visit despite your repeated no, the visit went wrong, and you kept the door shut on her. When you left for nursing school in September you stopped speaking to your mother, a silence that held for roughly a year. The shifts pile up around your grandmother's death and your move to nursing school, with the period settling as you began your nursing programme.

clusters.name: Jonah's marriage to Wren and shifts in his wider family, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: In March 2017 you married Wren; around the same time you saw your mother a bit less once she came along. That October your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. By 2018 your sister had wed and flown for a regional airline; your aunt Imogen's memory was slipping and she lashed out when muddled. In October 2019 your job steadied and paid well, easing your strain, but you felt constantly that you ought to be driving projects forward and started a sleeping pill. Around the same time Wren's family gathered at the lake for her mother's retirement; she was swamped by the run of events, you overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her, and at the lake weekend you were awake from the small hours with no more sleep, could only pull back as the others rose, and felt you didn't belong. The shifts pile up around your marriage, your aunt's decline, your sister's move away, and the gathering of Wren's family, with the period settling as you and Wren returned home and your anxiety eased with a regular pattern of shorter calls to your mother.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.
